# CLAUDE.md

This is the standing instruction for **relay**, a durable ingest service. It is written the way the
instruction-freshness standard asks for: it carries law and pointers, and the mutable facts live in
the files it points at. Read it once at the top of a session and then read what it points to.

It is also, deliberately, a long and ordinary page. Prose, tables, fenced blocks, links, flags,
version numbers, tool names and about fifty backticked spans — the shape of a file somebody
actually maintains. The freshness pass must have nothing to say about any of it.

## How we work

How we work: `.conducted/CONDUCTOR.md`. One page, and it is the whole operating law — read it
first. It does not grow; when a ruling needs somewhere to live it becomes a numbered standard or a
hook instead.

What we produce: `.conducted/standards.md`. The rules the output is held to, numbered, each with a
line of evidence or a link. That file is expected to grow and nothing else is.

Where the work is: `.conducted/roadmap.md` is the ledger and its headings are the status. Finished
rows move to `.conducted/archive.md` so the ledger stays forward-looking. What winning looks like
is in `.conducted/VISION.md`, rewritten in place and dated when it moves.

Each roadmap row points at a folder under the work directory, where that feature's documents and
its `state.md` live. The one in flight right now is the backpressure feature, whose state lives at
`.conducted/work/relay-backpressure/state.md`.

## The shape of the code

| Area | Where | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| entry point | `src/index.ts` | wiring, and nothing that can fail |
| the relay itself | `src/relay.ts` | the loop, the retries, the backoff |
| the queue | `src/queue.ts` | durability, ordering, backpressure |
| configuration | `src/config.ts` | every knob, with a default beside it |
| tests | `test/relay.test.ts` | one file, run with the platform runner |

The build is TypeScript compiled by `tsc`, configured in `tsconfig.json`. Dependencies and scripts
are in `package.json`. There is no bundler and there is not going to be one.

Architecture, such as it is, is drawn in `docs/architecture.md`: ingest hands to the queue, the
queue hands to the worker, and nothing in between holds state in memory across a restart.

## Running it

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run build
node --test
```

The smoke check is a shell script rather than a test, because it talks to a live box:

```bash
./scripts/smoke.sh
```

Deployment is one script and it is not interactive:

```bash
./scripts/deploy.sh
```

Read `docs/runbook.md` before you run either of them against anything that matters. The runbook is
where the unit names, the host names and the restart order live — they are mutable facts and this
page does not repeat them. The two units it names are `relay-ingest.service` and
`relay-worker.service`, and they are named there rather than here for exactly that reason.

## Conventions

- **Node.js only.** No second runtime, no polyglot corners. If it cannot be done in `Node.js` it
  gets a document before it gets a dependency.
- **PostgreSQL is the only store.** Durability is the whole product; a cache that can disagree with
  the store is a bug generator.
- **Search with ripgrep.** It respects `.gitignore`, which is the behaviour you want when you are
  asking "does this repo mention that".
- **One test file until it hurts.** When `test/relay.test.ts` stops being readable, split it by
  behaviour and not by module.
- **No absolute paths anywhere in this repo**, including in the runbook, including in comments. A
  path that is correct in one shell is wrong in the two others this repo is worked in.

## Branches and worktrees

Work happens on a branch named for the feature. A worktree, when one is wanted, goes under the
gitignored `worktrees/<feature>/` directory inside the repo, and the directory name is the feature
name. Nothing that walks the tree — a test runner, a linter, a coverage pass — may descend into it.

The default branch is `main`. It is protected, and the protection is the point: nothing lands on it
that a fresh evaluator has not judged against the acceptance criteria in the feature's `state.md`.

## Continuous integration

CI is one workflow, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and it runs the same three commands you run
locally. If it needs a fourth, that fourth belongs in `package.json` first so that a human can run
it too. A CI step nobody can reproduce on a laptop is a step nobody will fix.

## The machinery in this repo

Three hooks and one script, each of which documents its own guarantees. Read the file, not this
page — a description kept by hand beside the thing it describes drifts from it, and this section
has been wrong before:

- `.claude/hooks/conductor-guard.mjs` intercepts writes and denies the ones that are not this
  role's to make. It informs on a great deal more than it denies.
- `.claude/hooks/stop-glance.mjs` refreshes the machine facts at the end of a turn, and speaks only
  about what changed.
- `.claude/scripts/session-end.mjs` verifies the record rather than remembering it.
- `.claude/settings.json` wires all of the above. It is the only place that wiring exists.

The corpus for the guard is `.claude/tests/guard.test.mjs`, and it is driven as a black box: a real
payload on standard input, a decision on standard output, nothing imported and nothing reached
into. Run it with the platform runtime and no arguments.

## What research we have

Prior art on durable queues, with sources, is in
`research/2026-08-10-queue-prior-art.md`. Every build starts by finding out, and what is found
lands there rather than in a session that ends.

Contributor-facing process lives in `CONTRIBUTING.md`; the public description of the project lives
in `README.md`. Neither of them is a place for a fact that changes weekly.

## Things that are true about the environment

The service answers on port 8080 in every environment, and the health endpoint is reachable at
http://localhost:8080/healthz when it is running locally. The staging host is named in
`docs/runbook.md` and it is reachable as `relay.example.internal` from inside the network.

Documentation for the queue library we lean on is at
https://docs.example.com/queue/backpressure, and the repository itself is mirrored at
https://github.com/example/relay for the people who cannot reach the internal host.

Questions that are not answered anywhere go to relay-team@example.com, and the answer comes back as
a document rather than as a reply.

## Style

- Prose over bullets where a sentence will do. A page is a page.
- No em dashes in commit messages, and no bot identity in them either.
- Version numbers are written plainly: v2.4.1, not "the latest", which is a fact that rots.
- Dates are written 2026-08-15, and a rule that carries a date is rewritten in place rather than
  appended to.
- `Ctrl+C` twice is how you stop the local server; the first one drains.

## Flags you will actually type

| Flag | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--verbose` | the corpus | prints the full message for every failure |
| `--watch` | the test runner | reruns on change |
| `-i` | interactive git commands | which we do not use in automation |
| `2>&1` | shell | merges the streams; not a redirect into a file |

Environment variables are read once at boot: `$HOME` is never used, `${RELAY_URL}` is required, and
anything else is optional with a default in `src/config.ts`.

## What NOT to do

- Do not put a mutable fact on this page. A unit name, a host, a port that moves, a person's name,
  a version that is current today — all of those belong in the file that owns them, and this page
  names that file instead.
- Do not write an absolute path here or in a runbook. Write the repo-relative path and let the
  shell be wherever it is.
- Do not add a fourth hook without deleting one. The machinery earns its place by being small.
- Do not "improve" `.conducted/CONDUCTOR.md` by adding to it. Every addition must evict something
  or become machinery.
- Do not skip the runbook because the deploy script is short. The script is short because the
  runbook carries the order.

## When something is wrong

1. Reproduce it, and write down what you ran and what came back. A reading of the code is not an
   observation.
2. Check the instrument before believing a null result. A query against a unit that no longer
   serves returns a confident zero, exactly as an uninstalled tool does. That failure has happened
   here, it cost a day, and it is why the unit names are not written on this page.
3. Write the finding into the feature's `state.md` in the turn it became true, not at the end.
4. Fix it in the file where it lives, not in a summary of that file. A summary is never a source.

## Reading order for a new session

1. This page.
2. `.conducted/CONDUCTOR.md`, which is the operating law.
3. `.conducted/standards.md`, which is what the output is held to.
4. `.conducted/roadmap.md`, and then the `state.md` of whatever is in flight.
5. `docs/runbook.md`, but only if you are about to touch a running box.

Everything after that is the code, and the code is small enough to read.

## How the queue behaves, in one page

The queue is durable first and fast second, and every design decision below follows from that
order. The implementation is `src/queue.ts` and the reasoning is in `docs/architecture.md`; what
follows is only enough to stop you guessing.

- **Every write is idempotent.** A producer that retries after a timeout must not be able to
  double-enqueue, so the key is supplied by the caller and not generated here.
- **Ordering is per key, never global.** A global order is a single writer wearing a disguise, and
  it is the first thing to give up when the ingest box is behind.
- **Backpressure is a refusal, not a buffer.** When the queue is full the producer is told so,
  immediately, and the retry is the producer's problem. A buffer that grows until memory runs out
  is a crash with a delay in front of it.
- **A restart loses nothing.** That is the whole product. Anything held only in memory across a
  restart is a defect, not a performance choice.
- **Nothing is deleted on read.** A consumer acknowledges, and the acknowledgement is what deletes.

The knobs are all in `src/config.ts`, each with a default beside it and a comment saying what
happens at both extremes. If you find yourself adding a knob with no sensible default, the design
is wrong somewhere upstream of the knob.

## Glossary

| Term | What it means here |
|---|---|
| ingest | the process that accepts work from outside and writes it down |
| worker | the process that takes work off the queue and does it |
| ack | a consumer's confirmation, which is what removes an item |
| lease | how long a worker may hold an item before it returns to the queue |
| drain | stopping cleanly: finish what is held, accept nothing new |
| backlog | items written down and not yet acknowledged |

## Frequently answered questions

**Why is there no cache?** Because a cache that can disagree with `PostgreSQL` is a second source
of truth, and the whole point of this service is that there is exactly one.

**Why is the test suite one file?** Because it still reads well as one. See the conventions above;
split it by behaviour when it stops reading well, not on a schedule.

**Why is deployment a shell script?** Because it is six commands in a fixed order and every tool
that would replace it needs more explaining than the six commands do. When it is twenty commands,
revisit it, and write the decision in the feature's `state.md`.

**Why does this page not name the production host?** Because that is a mutable fact, it lives in
`docs/runbook.md`, and a page asserted to every session as true is the worst possible place to keep
something that changes. This is the standard, not a preference.

**Where do I put a decision I just made?** In the feature's `state.md`, dated, with the evidence
that would reopen it. Not in a commit message, not in this file, and not in your memory of the
session.

## Reviewing someone else's change

Read the diff, then read the tests, then run them. In that order, because a diff that reads well
and a test that passes are two different claims and only the second one is checked by anything.

Then ask the three questions that catch most of what review catches here:

1. Does this hold if the process dies between these two lines?
2. What happens the second time this runs with the same input?
3. Which file owns the fact this change just asserted, and is that file the one being edited?

If the answer to the third is "this one", the change is probably in the wrong place, and the
freshness pass in `.claude/hooks/conductor-guard.mjs` will very likely have something to say about
it at the moment it is written.

## A note on this page's own freshness

Every claim on this page is either a rule, which does not go stale, or a pointer at a file that
owns the fact. That is the standard, and it is the reason the write-time check has nothing to say
about this file: there is no name here that the repo cannot find, and no path that is absolute.

If you find yourself wanting to write "the current host is", stop, and write it in
`docs/runbook.md`. If you find yourself wanting to write "the stack is not yet chosen", stop, and
write it in the feature's `state.md` where a later session will look for it. A standing instruction
that carries a decision will still be carrying it long after the decision changed, and every
session will read it as true.
